bullets.title: Semis log 5-6 consecutive down days; SOX -1.8% pre-mkt on CXMT/AI financing fears
bullets.body: The semiconductor selloff is entering its 5th-6th straight session, matching the longest streak since the Spring 2025 Liberation Day event. China's CXMT claims a DDR5 4F² DRAM cell breakthrough ~2 years ahead of Samsung's roadmap (commercial skepticism remains but major equipment suppliers Daifuku/TEL/Kokusai are seeing aggressive order ramps). Separately, AVGO CEO Hock Tan warned AI capital deployment 'resembles casino gambling' with borrowing costs now a bigger constraint than chips, while JPMorgan and Goldman rejected $3.7B of a Volta AI loan tranche on risk concerns.

bullets.title: Korea KOSPI -5.5% overnight, -33.8% from June peak; Asia semis routed
bullets.body: South Korea's KOSPI fell 5.5% Monday night and is down 33.8% from June highs amid AI bubble deflation fears. Samsung and SK Hynix fell 8-10%; Japan's Nikkei dropped 1.8% with Kioxia down 13%. Hedgeye is positioned short semis/DRAM and long software, looking to short bounces.

bullets.title: 10-yr yield at 5.19%; SPX futures +0.10% despite tech drag; lightest SPY volume since Nov 2005
bullets.body: The 10-year Treasury sits at 5.19% with SPY trading at 18.6M shares yesterday — the lightest volume since November 2005, with broader index volumes down 25%. S&P futures are slightly positive at 7849.75 even as NDX futures are down ~70bps, reflecting rotation out of tech/semis. Major US banks are entering correction territory as Treasury yields surge.

bullets.title: September CPI today: GS expects core +0.24% m/m / +2.46% y/y; headline +0.59% on energy
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs previews September CPI with core at +0.24% m/m and +2.46% y/y, while headline prints hotter at +0.59% m/m / +3.70% y/y driven by energy. The quality factor is increasingly punitive in the current credit environment, with reversal risk flagged around today's CPI release and the upcoming Fed meeting.

bullets.title: AI capex supersycle intact: JPM raises cloud DC capex to +85% in 2026 ($270B+), +70% in 2027 ($400B+)
bullets.body: JPM's latest data center capex model projects the largest annual step-up in a decade: top-4 U.S. CSPs (Google +120%, Meta +100%, Amazon +70%, Microsoft +55%) collectively spending $270B+ in 2026 and $400B+ in 2027, consuming 80% and 111% of operating cash flow respectively. Installed North American capacity expands from 54 GW (2025) to 125 GW (2027), with planned capacity already at 200 GW+. JPM is bullish on networking suppliers as the gating factor for high-end compute.

bullets.title: MSFT Maia 300 targets 1M+ chip deployment by 2027, reducing NVDA dependence structurally
bullets.body: Microsoft unveiled its Maia 300 AI inference chip with 40% better power efficiency vs. GPUs, with analysts projecting 500K-1M+ units shipped in 2027. Citi flagged that the Maia XPU ramp magnitude is not yet fully reflected in Marvell's revenue framework, suggesting upside. MSFT is also reshaping Azure leadership amid cloud/AI reorganization.

bullets.title: META Muse Wonder launch drives stock +40% off lows; needs 2027 capex/opex KPIs to break to $800+
bullets.body: Meta released Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, described as frontier-level models competitive with Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, and Gemini 4 Argon, priced at $4-$20/M tokens. Stock is up ~40% off lows with investor sentiment described as 'white hot.' JPM's Q3 preview sees revenue at ~$64B (+26% y/y) at the high end of guidance, but notes the stock needs concrete Muse KPIs (DAUs, downloads) and a 2027 opex/capex surprise ($210-225B opex vs Street $203B; $225-250B capex vs Street $200B) to break to $800+.

bullets.title: AI/Semi crowding at 7/10 vs. 10/10 at June peak; BofA FMS shows 37% of managers OW tech, highest since Aug 2020
bullets.body: AI/semis positioning has pulled back to ~7 out of 10 crowding versus 10 out of 10 at the June 22 peak, per Jefferies. BofA's October Fund Manager Survey separately flags 37% of managers overweight tech — the highest proportion since August 2020 — and global investors most exposed to tech stocks since 2020, raising reversal risk. Retail single-stock options volume has risen to 2021 meme-stock levels.

bullets.title: GOOGL Q3: GCP likely +105-115% Y/Y on TPU sales; Cloud on path to match Search revenue by late 2028
bullets.body: JPM's GOOGL preview sees Search revenue +14% Y/Y with consensus concerns overblown, while Google Cloud is the bigger story at +105-115% Y/Y driven by TPU sales. Cloud EBIT margins are the critical focus — if they beat Street's ~33% estimate, it validates strong TPU economics. JPM models GOOGL 2027 Capex at $330-350B vs. Street's ~$305B.

bullets.title: ASML (Wed) and TSMC (Thu) earnings are the critical semi read this week
bullets.body: ASML reports Wednesday pre-open and is expected to guide flat with Q3 revenue of €11.7B and gross margins of 56.4%; Jefferies maintains Hold. TSMC reports Thursday and UBS is raising 2027-28 capex forecasts; Jefferies estimates N2/N3 utilization above 100% in 2027 driving 10%+ wafer price increases. Both prints are viewed as pivotal for validating or refuting the AI capex thesis.

bullets.title: Power scarcity is the binding AI infrastructure constraint; 19 GW shortages projected next year
bullets.body: 19 GW of power shortages are projected for next year with only ~12.9 GW of new data center capacity expected in 2026 and 18 GW in 2027, far below the 65 GW under construction and 361 GW announced. The powered-shell sector (HUT, APLD, CIFR, GLXY flagged as top beneficiaries) has contracted 5.9 GW of HPC with 38 GW+ in pipeline, yet shares are down 27% on average over the past 3 months. Lease rates are trending up 15%+ at new renewals per APLD.

bullets.title: Middle East: IMF models $130/bbl adverse scenario; Jefferies flags AI/hyperscalers as second strategic chokepoint
bullets.body: Jefferies geopolitical analysis warns Yemen has returned to full-scale war with U.S.-Iran diplomacy active but sequencing obstacles unresolved. The IMF adverse scenario assumes Hormuz stays closed into Q1 2027, pushing oil to $130/bbl, cutting 2027 global growth by 0.5pp and raising inflation by 1.1pp to 5.2%. Saudi Arabia's GDP is now forecast to contract 3.3% vs. a prior +1.7% estimate. Hyperscalers now account for ~10% of global IG bond issuance vs. <1% in 2024, directly linking AI investment to financial stability risk.

bullets.title: Fed expected to hike 1-3 more times through end-2026/27; quality factor punitive, reversal risk near CPI
bullets.body: JPM and JPM's China strategy both flag expectations for 1-3 additional Fed hikes through end-2026/early 2027, adding downward pressure on risk multiples globally. The quality factor is at an elevated and punitive level in current credit conditions, with JPM flagging reversal risk around the CPI print and upcoming Fed meeting. Short-term business loan rates have already jumped to 8.2% from 7.5% per the NFIB survey.

bullets.title: Small biz optimism cools; inflation re-accelerating with price-raising plans at highest since June
bullets.body: NFIB small business optimism slipped again in September — expected business conditions fell 4 points to net 6% (lowest since May), capex plans hit lowest since June, and profit trends declined to net -20% with 34% citing weaker sales. Price-raising plans rose to net 31%, the highest since June, while 24% cited rising material costs (up 8 points from August). AI data-center demand is being cited as a driver of aluminum cost pressure for manufacturers.

bullets.title: JPM/WFC earnings worse than expected; bank earnings season kicks off with breadth concerns
bullets.body: JPMorgan and Wells Fargo posted earnings and guidance worse than expected, contributing to overnight weakness. JPM's morning briefing is nonetheless tactically bullish on earnings season broadening, with 26Q3 EPS growth expected at +29.6% and all 11 S&P sectors showing positive growth. IT budget growth expectations rose to +4.0% in 2026 from +3.8% in the prior CIO survey, with AI/ML remaining the #1 priority and most defensible spending category.

bullets.title: France fiscal crisis: yields spiking, corporate debt highest in Europe, ECB response uncertain
bullets.body: PSC Macro flags France as 'the newest peripheral' with taxes and spending exceeding 50% of GDP, French non-financial corporate debt more than double the U.S. ratio and the highest among European peers. Rising yields are a headwind to sub-1% growth forecasts, and ECB policy response (pause, ease, or QE) depends on how far contagion spreads. French asset underperformance expected to continue.

bullets.title: OCP Day 1: Inference now #1 AI workload; agentic token usage up 14x YTD, $1.4T accelerator TAM by 2030
bullets.body: JPM's OCP Day 1 takeaways show inference has overtaken training as the #1 AI workload due to agentic adoption, with agentic token usage up more than 14x YTD. Data center AI accelerator TAM is projected to grow at >45% CAGR from $200B (2025) to $1.4T (2030). NVIDIA Spectrum-X Photonics CPO achieves 5x higher power efficiency; AMD's Helion agentic AI rack is ramping at OpenAI, Meta, Anthropic, Microsoft, and Oracle.

bullets.title: WFE spending could double to $500B by 2030; AMAT Investor Day to reveal 25-30% CAGR guide
bullets.body: UBS previews Applied Materials' Investor Day as likely to show a 25-30%+ WFE spending CAGR through 2030, with gross margins targeting the mid-50% range. WFE spending could rise from the current $280-300B toward $500B by 2030. AMAT CEO also plans to double revenue without commensurate headcount growth via AI tools for R&D, quality control, and yield optimization.

bullets.title: China A-shares AI sub-sectors down 14-17% in 5 days; JPM maintains barbell, CSI-300 target 5,200
bullets.body: JPM's China A-share strategy notes AI sub-sectors are down 14-17% over the past 5 trading days as geopolitical concerns (FCC rules, MATCH Act, import limits) weigh on valuations, though supply constraints through 2028 provide cushion. CSI-300 IT companies are delivering +53% FTM EPS y/y. JPM maintains a barbell of high-yield defensives plus AI infrastructure/CXO/innovative drugs, with a CSI-300 year-end 2026 target of 5,200.

bullets.title: Character.ai files Chapter 11; Disney is stalking horse bidder at $20M for IP license
bullets.body: Character.ai initiated voluntary Chapter 11 bankruptcy in Delaware. Disney will serve as stalking horse bidder for a non-exclusive perpetual license of Character.ai IP and claims for $20M, with sale process completion expected late November or early December 2026. This reflects the pressure on standalone consumer AI companies as frontier model costs escalate.
